findings.claim: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the requireNonNull call with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and gets encoded as '<prefix>:null', or causes a later NPE.

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73, the constructor checks Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed") and then checks grantType a second time on line 73 with Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of rawTokenId. Consequently, a null rawTokenId is accepted and concatenated into '<prefix>:null' in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:114-117 or left null for downstream callers.

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for prefixes shorter than 5 characters instead of returning false.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:480-483, isAccessTokenId splits item on ':' and only checks items.length != 2 before calling items[0].substring(3, 5). Because items[0].length() is never validated, any colon-separated value whose prefix has fewer than 5 characters throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5). The grant shortcut sits at positions 4-5 of the 2+2+2 prefix, so the correct call is substring(4, 6).

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483, isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut using items[0].substring(3, 5), whereas services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:79-81 encodes the 6-char prefix as 2+2+2 and reads the grant shortcut with encodedContext.substring(4, 6).

findings.claim: The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic: it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected grant shortcut, so it rejects correct tokens and accepts wrong grant shortcuts.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:483, isAccessTokenId checks if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; without negation. It therefore returns false when the extracted value equals expectedGrantShortcut and falls through to return isUUID().matches(items[1]) for non-matching grant shortcuts.

findings.claim: The Dependabot label 'area/dependencies' does not exist.

verifier.reason: Although `area/dependencies` is configured in `.github/dependabot.yml:12` and `.github/dependabot.yml:23` and referenced in `.github/teams.yml:55` (with `dependencies` listed as an area in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml:43`), GitHub repository labels are not defined or synced by files in this repository. Determining whether the `area/dependencies` label actually exists in the GitHub repository requires checking the external GitHub service and cannot be settled from the source code alone.

findings.claim: The lazy/hot-deploy refresh paths in getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 106-137) add entries without the duplicate-shortcut check that postInit performs, so a custom grant can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping.

verifier.reason: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java, both lazy refresh methods—getShortcutByGrantType (lines 106-119) and getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 121-137)—insert directly into grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts via put() without the duplicate-shortcut validation performed by postInit (lines 82-85). Specifically, line 113 unconditionally overwrites any existing shortcut entry in grantsByShortcuts if a newly deployed custom grant reuses an existing shortcut.

findings.claim: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, and the patch uses both inconsistently: OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, while grants and TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE.

verifier.reason: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/Constants.java:207 defines GRANT_TYPE as a direct alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, and the patch mixes both: OAuth2GrantType.java:102 reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE from formParams while OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.java:134, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.java:82, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237, and TokenManager.java:248 write Constants.GRANT_TYPE to clientSessionCtx.
